Description

Error 500 returned by the endpoint:

GET https://apil.gothru.co/v1/tours/status/extra-pano?mid=3491846
Request Method GET
Status Code 500 Internal Server Error

Response payload

{
    "statusCode": 500,
    "data": {
        "messages": "An error occurred (google photos): {\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": 403,\n    \"message\": \"Request had insufficient authentication scopes.\",\n    \"errors\": [\n      {\n        \"message\": \"Insufficient Permission\",\n        \"domain\": \"global\",\n        \"reason\": \"insufficientPermissions\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"status\": \"PERMISSION_DENIED\",\n    \"details\": [\n      {\n        \"@type\": \"type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo\",\n        \"reason\": \"ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT\",\n        \"domain\": \"googleapis.com\",\n        \"metadata\": {\n          \"service\": \"streetviewpublish.googleapis.com\",\n          \"method\": \"google.streetview.publish.v1.StreetViewPublishService.ListPhotos\"\n        }\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n"
    }
}

Analysis

The underlying Google API returns a 403 PERMISSION_DENIED / ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT for streetviewpublish.googleapis.com -> StreetViewPublishService.ListPhotos. The OAuth access token used to call the Street View Publish API is missing the required scope (https://www.googleapis.com/auth/streetviewpublish).

Two problems to address:

  1. Scope issue: The Google account/token used for this request lacks the Street View Publish scope (token needs re-consent/refresh with the correct scope, or the wrong account is linked).
  2. Error handling: A downstream 403 from Google is surfaced to the client as an unhandled 500. The endpoint should map the Google permission error to a proper status (e.g. 403/4xx) with a clear, actionable message instead of a generic 500.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. The endpoint GET /v1/tours/status/extra-pano?mid=... no longer returns a 500 when the Google Street View Publish token has insufficient scope.
  2. Insufficient-scope / permission errors from Google are caught and returned with an appropriate status code and a clear message prompting re-authentication.
  3. Re-authenticating the Google account with the correct streetviewpublish scope resolves the underlying 403 and the endpoint returns valid data.

Reference: docs/brainstom/analyze-all.md - Google Street View Publisher API dependency is flagged as the platform's highest-severity risk (§6.2). Relates to OAuth scope handling for Street View publishing.

This error occurs because the street view account is not connected to the gothru account,,, but the error was too general before, but I have fixed it to be like this

issues.display_title: Issue #1294: Bug Fix: API Error Responses Expose SQL Queries
issues.main_description_html:
Acceptance Criteria

AC-1 — Database errors show a friendly message, not SQL

Given the database is unreachable when a user performs any action (e.g. uploading a tour)
When the app receives the error response
Then the user sees "Service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later." — no SQL query, no database details, no error codes

AC-2 — Any other unexpected error also shows a friendly message

Given an unhandled server error occurs on any endpoint
When the app receives the error response
Then the user sees "Oops! Something went wrong. Please try again later." — no stack traces, no file paths, no internal details

AC-3 — Errors are still visible to the engineering team

Given a database or unexpected error occurs
When the server handles it
Then the full error details (including SQL, stack trace, file path) are written to the server logs — nothing is lost for debugging

AC-4 — Normal API responses are unchanged

Given a request that succeeds, or fails with a known business error (e.g. "not owner", "invalid token")
When the app receives the response
Then the response is identical to before this fix — no change to any existing message or status code

issues.main_description_html:
Brainstorming File:
2026-06-02-list-tours-v1-has-main-overlay-design.md

Acceptance Criteria

AC-1 — File exists → has_main_overlay: true

Given a tour whose overlay.json exists at /data/moderation/{userId}/{1_cid}/overlay/{tourId}/overlay.json
When GET /v1/tours/list is called
Then that tour item in the response contains "has_main_overlay": true

AC-2 — File absent → has_main_overlay: false

Given a tour that has never been saved in the overlay editor (no overlay.json file on disk)
When GET /v1/tours/list is called
Then that tour item contains "has_main_overlay": false

AC-3 — No overlay record → has_main_overlay: false

Given a tour that has no row in hosted_tours.tours (getTourOverlayInfo() returns null or tour_id is 0)
When GET /v1/tours/list is called
Then that tour item contains "has_main_overlay": false (no filesystem check is attempted)

AC-4 — has_main_overlay is independent of overlay_active

Given a tour that has an overlay.json on disk but foverlay_active is not '1' (overlay configured but not published)
When GET /v1/tours/list is called
Then the response contains "overlay_active": false AND "has_main_overlay": true simultaneously

And given a tour where foverlay_active is '1' (published) but the overlay.json file has been deleted from disk
Then the response contains "overlay_active": true AND "has_main_overlay": false simultaneously

AC-5 — Field is always present

Given any tour in the list (with or without overlay info)
When GET /v1/tours/list is called
Then every tour item includes has_main_overlay as a boolean — never absent, never null

AC-6 — Encrypted response also includes the field

Given a request with enc: true header
When GET /v1/tours/list returns an encrypted envelope
Then the decrypted list_tours array still contains has_main_overlay in each tour item (the field is set at the Action level, before encryption)
